extracted.intended_audience: researchers (especially early-career) preparing to serve as journal peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: A short training course for researchers on how to perform journal peer reviews: what to avoid, how to write effective review reports, and how reviewing can support career development toward editorial roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not accept a review if you don't have time
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid saying yes when you don’t have time to complete a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course explicitly warns reviewers not to accept invitations they cannot complete — accepting without time risks missing deadlines or producing low-quality reviews, which disadvantages editors and authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid biased or unfair statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not provide biased or unfair statements in your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain impartiality and fairness; avoid ad hominem comments, unjustified criticism, or allowing personal bias to shape evaluation. The modules call out biased/unfair statements as actions to definitely avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be constructive in your feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide constructive feedback that helps authors improve their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course emphasises explaining how to be constructive in feedback — give actionable suggestions, cite evidence, and balance criticism with positive comments so reports are useful to authors and editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider each element of the article when reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight points to consider when looking at each element of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should systematically evaluate elements of the manuscript (as covered in the 'How to review a manuscript' module). The module outlines which parts of the paper to examine and what questions to ask for each element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn common reviewing mistakes (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of common reviewing mistakes so you can avoid them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course includes material on common mistakes and a webinar titled '10 tips for writing a truly terrible review' that uses anti-pattern examples to show what not to do.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow tips for writing an effective review
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt best-practice tips for writing clear, effective review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The programme promises practical tips (tone, structure, clarity, actionable recommendations) in the 'Tips for writing an effective review' materials and webinar to help produce reports that meet editors' needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reviewing activities to support career development
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognise that reviewing can provide a stepping stone towards becoming a journal editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course covers insights into how reviewing can boost your career and includes a module 'How reviewers become editors' describing how consistent, high-quality reviewing contributes to editorial opportunities.
